entry.name: mcwrapper-group
entry.digest: Messages and attributes common to MC wrapper objects
entry.description: The MC wrapper defines common messages and attributes for all compatible objects.

attributes.name: annotation

attributes.name: background
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: busymapname
attributes.digest: Busy Map Name
attributes.description: When theattribute is enabled, an MC wrapper object uses the local busy map of anyorin the same patcher by default. To use a named global busy map instead, set theattribute to the desired name. For brevity the name @bzname can also be used.

attributes.name: chans
attributes.digest: Number of channels
attributes.description: Theattribute sets the number of channels and instances in the MC wrapper object. To define a fixed number of channels regardless of what is connected to the object, setvia a typed-in argument, for example typingwould create 100 instances of aobject inside the MC wrapper. Ifis 0, the wrapper object will auto-adapt to the number of channels in its input multichannel signals (using the maximum of all connected signals). If an object does not have any multichannel signals connected to its inlets, theattribute will need to have a non-zero value if you want more than one instance.Ifis changed while the audio is on, the number of instances will not change until audio is restarted. However, ifis reduced while the audio is on, any extra channels will no longer process audio and will output a zero signal.

attributes.name: initialvalues
attributes.digest: Assign initial values (arguments) for each instance
attributes.description: Theattribute only applies to object creation time so it must be set via a typed-in argument.sets the first (and only the first) initial argument for successive instances in the MC wrapper. For example, typingwould assign an initial frequency to theinstances inside the wrapper. The first instance would be assigned a frequency of 50, the second a frequency of 60, the third 70, and the fourth 80. Note thatdoes not determine the actual instance count; this can be done using theattribute. If there are more instances than elements for theattribute, those instances are instantiated with the default value.To set a default value of an argument for all instances, type it as an argument before any typed-in attributes. For example, modifying our example above:. In this example, the first four instances are set as before, but the next six are created with a frequency argument of 100.To change instance values or attributes after the wrapper object has been created, use the,, ormessages.

attributes.name: replicate
attributes.digest: Replicate input channels to fill the content of all expected channels
attributes.description: Whenis enabled, input single-channel or multichannel signals containing fewer channels than the number instances in the MC wrapper object are repeated to fill all input channels. For example, whenis enabled and you connect a two-channel multichannel signal to the input of an MC wrapper object with four instances, channel 1 of the input will be repeated to channel 3, and channel 2 of the input will be repeated to channel 4. Ifwere disabled, channels 3 and 4 of the input would be set to zero.

attributes.name: size
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: target
attributes.digest: Set channel for incoming messages
attributes.description: Theattribute sets an index for targeting specific wrapper instances. Subsequent messages are directed to an individual instance instead of all instances. It is strongly recommended you use the more reliablemessage instead of theattribute. The voice index ofwill override the current setting of. Whenis 0, incoming messages are sent to all instances. Whenis -1, incoming messages do nothing. Note thatonly affects messages, not setting attribute values.

attributes.name: usebusymap
attributes.digest: Use busy map
attributes.description: Whenis enabled, the MC wrapper controls whether individual instances process audio using amaintained by either anorobject. When a channel in the busy map is marked as "free" or "released" no audio processing occurs by any instance on the channel corresponding to the voice index. Whenis disabled, instances in the MC wrapper process audio at all times. This will also be true ifis enabled and there is no local or named busy map available. (See theattribute for a description of local and named busy maps). For brevity the namecan also be used.

attributes.digest: Assign initial values (arguments) for each instance
attributes.description: You can useas an alternate name for theattribute.

attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: voiceprob
attributes.digest: Assign setvalue probability for * and $
attributes.description: Theattribute is used when employing the $ or * arguments to themessage. It determines the probability that themessage will be sent. For example, ifis 0.9, there is a 90% chance the setvalue message will be sent to a randomly chosen voice.

attributes.name: zero
attributes.digest: Zero unused outputs
attributes.description: When theattribute is enabled, channels in the MC wrapper due to the use of a busy map output zero signals. To save a small amount of CPU at the risk of loud and unpleasant noises due to uncleared signal data, you can disable. In this case, disabled channels in the MC wrapper do nothing to their output channels. Ifis disabled or there is no active local or named busy map available, the setting of theattribute has no effect.Conveniently, whenis enabled inobject, disabled channels are not mixed to the output. When unused signals from wrapped objects withdisabled feed into, they will be ignored, reducing the risk of unpleasantness getting past the mix output.

messages.name: applymessages
messages.digest: Send messages to multiple channels
messages.description: The word, followed by one or more numbers and/or symbols, sends individual messages successively to instances in the MC wrapper, starting with the first instance. For example, the messagewill send the '0' message to the first instance, and the 'bang' message to the second instance. If there are more instances than arguments to, the extra instances are unaffected.

messages.name: applynvalues
messages.digest: Set multiple values for multiple channels
messages.description: Whereascan only set one value, the messagepermits sending a message or setting an attribute with multiple values to instances in the MC wrapper, starting with the first instance. This is helpful for messages that require multiple values, such as the list message toto set start/end points. The message syntax is [applynvalues N value1, value2 etc.] where N is the number of values to set for each instance. For example, the messagewill send 500 600 to the first instance and 900 1000 to the second instance. If there are more instances than specified in, the extra instances are unaffected.

messages.name: applyvalues
messages.digest: Set values for multiple channels
messages.description: The word, followed by an optional message name and one or more message arguments, sends individual values in the arguments successively to instances in the MC wrapper, starting with the first instance. For example, the messagewill send 4 to the first instance, 5 to the second instance, and 6 to the third instance. If there are more instances than arguments to, the extra instances are unaffected.

messages.name: decide
messages.digest: Generate random on-off values for all channels
messages.description: Themessage generates a uniformly distributed random value between 0 and 1 for each channel; if the value is less than the probability value set by the first argument, the second argument is assigned to the channel. If the random value is greater than the probability value, 0 is asigned to the channel. (If a second argument is not present, 1 is used by default.)Example:for four channels would generate 0, 0, 0, 0 because the probability of generating a 1 is zero.could generate 10, 0, 0, 10 if the randomly generated values exceeded 0.5 for the first and fourth channels.If no message name is provided, amessage is used by default.

messages.name: deviate
messages.digest: Generate a random value for each channel around a center value
messages.description: Generate a random value for each channel around a center value. An optional number after the center value specifies the upper range size so it can be different from the lower range size.Example:will generate random values for theattribute of the objects in the wrapper centered around 1000 Hz (between 900 and 1100 Hz).sendsmessages to the objects in the wrapper with random values between 900 and 1200.If no message name is provided, amessage is used by default.

messages.name: ease.linear
messages.digest: Apply an easing function
messages.description: The MC wrapper provides access to the easing functions found in the Ease Package. These are accessed with message names consisting ofconcatenated with the easing function name. For example, to use thefunction, send the message.Themessages generate an non-linear and inclusive range of values across the space of channels. When you use two number arguments, the first value will be the low end of the range and the second will be the high end of the range. Forandfunctions, this means the low end value will be set for the first channel and the high end will be set for the last channel. Forfunction variants, the high end will be set for the first channel and the low end will be set for the last channel.When themessages are supplied with three numerical arguments, the first two specify the range as in the two-argument case, but the third argument, which will be constrained between 0 and 1, defines a mid point. Between the first channel and the channel closest to the mid point, the entire range of the function is applied. Between the mid point and the last channel, the range of the function is applied with the values reversed, creating a mirror image. The mirror image is exact when the third argument is 0.5, otherwise it will be biased toward 0 or 1. With a mid point of 1, the result is the same as if the third argument was not supplied at all. With a mid point of 0, the result is the same as if it was entirely reversed. In other words, it's as if theversion of the function were used instead of theversion that was originally specified -- or vice versa.Available messages are:,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,, and. Refer to the Ease Package documentation for details on these functions and demonstrations of their behavior.If no message name is provided, amessage is used by default.

messages.name: exponential
messages.digest: Generate an exponential series across all channels
messages.description: Themessage generates an exponential series. The first argument isand the second (optional) argument isin the following expression:where channel starts at 0 for the first channel.If the second argument is not present the default value is 1. Example:would generate, for four channels, values of 10, 3.678, 1.353, and 0.498.would generate 2, 5.437, 14.78, and 40.17.If no message name is provided, amessage is used by default.

messages.name: generate
messages.digest: Run a named generator function
messages.description: Themessage runs the function whose name is stored in theattribute. Arguments passed towill be given to the function that is called. Example: ifis set to,is the same as sending the message.

messages.name: harmonic
messages.digest: Generate a harmonic series across all channels
messages.description: Themessage generates a harmonic series using the second argument as the fundamental frequency () and the first argument as a multiplier () in the following expression:where channel starts at 0 for the first channel.Example:for five channels would generate 440, 880, 1320, 1760, and 2200.for four channels would generate 440, 660, 880, and 1100.If no message name is provided, amessage is used by default.

messages.name: increment
messages.digest: Generate a increasing value for each channel starting at a specified value
messages.description: Themessage generates a range of increasing values for each channel. The range starts at the second argument and increments each channel's value by the first argument. If no message name is provided then amessage is used by default.Example:for four channels would generate 2, 7, 12, and 17.If no message name is provided, amessage is used by default.

messages.name: randomrange
messages.digest: Generate a range of random values
messages.description: Themessage generates a uniformly distributed random range of values for all channels between the first argument and the second argument.If no message name is provided, amessage is used by default.

messages.name: replicatenvalues
messages.digest: Set multiple values for all channels
messages.description: Whereascan only set one value, the messagepermits sending a message or setting an attribute with multiple values to instances in the MC wrapper, starting with the first instance. This is helpful for messages that require multiple values, such as the list message toto set start/end points. The message syntax is [replicatenvalues N value1, value2 etc.] where N is the number of values to set for each instance. Unlike, themessage continues sending values to successive instances, restarting with the first group, if it runs out of arguments to send. For example,to an MC wrapper object with three instances will send 500 600 to the first instance, 900 1000 to the second instance, and 500 600 to the third instance.

messages.name: replicatevalues
messages.digest: Set values for all channels
messages.description: The word, followed by an optional message name and one or more message arguments, sends individual values in the arguments successively to instances in the MC wrapper, starting with the first instance. Unlike, themessage continues sending values to successive instances, restarting with the first element, if it runs out of arguments to send. For example,to an MC wrapper object with three instances will send 4 to the first instance, 5 to the second instance, and 4 to the third instance.

messages.name: scaledexponential
messages.digest: Generate a scaled exponential series across all channels
messages.description: Themessage generates an exponential series with the exponent scaled by the total number of channels. The first argument isand the second (optional) argument isin the following expression:where channel starts at 0 for the first channel.If the second argument is not present the default value is 1. Example:would generate, for six channels, values of 2, 2.363, 2.791, 3.297, 3.895, 4.602.for four channels would generate 2, 2.568, 3.297, 4.324.provides a way to keep the range of the exponential series roughly the same independent of the number of channels.If no message name is provided, amessage is used by default.

messages.name: setvalue
messages.digest: Direct a message to an individual channel
messages.description: The word, followed by both a channel index (starting at 1) and any message that can be sent to the wrapped object, sends the message to an individual instance within the MC wrapper., followed by a message, sends the message to all instances. Themessage can be used in any inlet.Instead of a number, themessage can also take a symbol indicating that the target channel index should be randomly chosen:

messages.name: setvaluerange
messages.digest: Send a message to a range of channels
messages.description: The word, followed by a low and high channel index (starting at 1) and any message that can be sent to the wrapped object, sends the message to the specified range of channels.Example:, sends the message 50 to channels 1 - 4. If the second argument is -1, the message is sent to all subsequent channels. For example,sends the message 50 to all channels between 2 and the current number of voices.Note: the random channel selection feature using,,, anddoes not work with themessage.
messages.argPattern: low channel:int, high channel:int, message:symbol, message arguments:list?

messages.name: smoothstep
messages.digest: Apply a smoothstep function
messages.description: Thefunction works analogously to themessages to generate an inclusive non-linear range of values, but uses thefunction to generate a non-linear ramp. Refer to the documentation of themessages for more information.If no message name is provided, amessage is used by default.

messages.name: spread
messages.digest: Generate a range of values distributed to each channel
messages.description: Themessage generates a range of values distributed to each channel. The first boundary value is included in the range outputs, but the second boundary value is not (see,, andfor other options).Example:for four channels would generate 0, 2.5, 5, and 7.5.If no message name is provided, amessage is used by default.By default the generated values are linearly distributed. If the optional exponent argument is present and greater than 0, the generated values are exponentially distributed.

messages.name: spreadexclusive
messages.digest: Generate a range of values distributed to each channel
messages.description: Themessage generates a range of values distributed to each channel. Neither the first and second boundary values are included in the range outputs.Example:for four channels would generate 2, 4, 6, and 8.If no message name is provided, amessage is used by default.By default the generated values are linearly distributed. If the optional exponent argument is present and greater than 0, the generated values are exponentially distributed.

messages.name: spreadincludefirst
messages.digest: Generate a range of values distributed to each channel
messages.description: Themessage generates a range of values distributed to each channel. It is the same as themessage. The first boundary value is included in the range outputs, but the second boundary value is not.Example:for four channels would generate 0, 2.5, 5, and 7.5.If no message name is provided, amessage is used by default.By default the generated values are linearly distributed. If the optional exponent argument is present and greater than 0, the generated values are exponentially distributed.

messages.name: spreadincludesecond
messages.digest: Generate a range of values distributed to each channel
messages.description: Themessage generates a range of values distributed to each channel. The first boundary value is not included in the range outputs, but the second boundary value is included.Example:for four channels would generate 2.5, 5, 7.5, and 10.If no message name is provided, amessage is used by default.By default the generated values are linearly distributed. If the optional exponent argument is present and greater than 0, the generated values are exponentially distributed.

messages.name: spreadinclusive
messages.digest: Generate a range of values distributed to each channel
messages.description: Themessage generates a range of values distributed to each channel. Both the first and second boundary values are included in the range outputs.Example:for four channels would generate 0, 3.33, 6.66, and 10.If no message name is provided, amessage is used by default.By default the generated values are linearly distributed. If the optional exponent argument is present and greater than 0, the generated values are exponentially distributed.

messages.name: subharmonic
messages.digest: Generate a subharmonic series across all channels
messages.description: Themessage generates a subharmonic series using the second argument as the fundamental frequency () and the first argument as a multiplier () in the following expression:where channel starts at 0 for the first channel.Example:for five channels would generate 440, 220, 146.7, and 110.If no message name is provided, amessage is used by default.
